title: radio.py: start_tx None (duty cycle) crashes; node stuck TX
description:
## Problem

`SimulationBase` constructs `Medium()` with the library default `enforce_duty_cycle=True` (EU868 1% / 36 s per hour). `Medium.start_tx` returns `None` when a new TX would exceed that budget (`lora_medium/medium.py`).

`RadioMixin._do_start_transmission` never checks for None. It mutates node/radio state *before* `start_tx`, then dereferences `tx.id`:

```python
self._medium.end_tx(previous_tx_id)          # previous airtime aborted
self._pending_rx_timeouts.pop(node_id, None)
self._cancel_rx_timeout_events(node_id)
self._drop_delayed_rx_for_receiver(node_id)
node.state = NodeState.TX
node.rx_callbacks = None
tx = self._medium.start_tx(...)              # None at 1%
self._active_transmissions[node_id] = tx.id  # AttributeError
```

Consequences once a node has used ~36 s of SF10 airtime in a 1-hour window (city-mesh, soak, 500-node demo):

1. **Crash.** `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'id'` aborts the sim/HIL loop.
2. **Stuck TX.** The exception happens after `node.state = TX` and after RX teardown. No `TxEndEvent` is queued, `_active_transmissions` is not updated, so the node never returns to IDLE.
3. **Half-duplex abort is not rolled back.** A replacement TX that is duty-cycle rejected has already `end_tx`'d the previous in-flight frame and dropped this receiver's delayed-RX stash.

This is not 9098.25 (RX during own airtime). It is not TDMA `is_tx_allowed` (that path returns `""` *before* mutating RX). Duty-cycle rejection is the only `start_tx` None path and is unhandled.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (`_do_start_transmission` pre-TX teardown + `tx.id` with no None check)
- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/base.py (`self._medium = Medium()` default enforce=True)
- python/.venv/.../lora_medium/medium.py (`start_tx` returns None; `enforce_duty_cycle=True`)

## Why this is robustness

Regulatory duty-cycle enforcement is on by default. Long runs are supposed to stay up and report duty-cycle pressure (`Metrics.set_duty_cycle`, dashboard). Instead they crash and leave a node in TX with no way to recover except `remove_node`.
design: Check `tx is None` immediately after `start_tx`. On reject: do not set NodeState.TX, do not abort a previous in-flight TX, do not tear down RX/stash, do not queue TxEndEvent, return "" (same as TDMA deny). Prefer calling start_tx *before* half-duplex teardown so a reject cannot destroy a live RX window or a previous TX. Tests: with Medium(enforce_duty_cycle=True), fill the 1% window, then start_transmission must return "" and leave state IDLE (or previous TX running) with no exception; a subsequent TX after the window slides must succeed.
acceptance_criteria: Filling a node's EU868 1% window then calling start_transmission does not raise. Node is not left in TX without a TxEndEvent. Previous in-flight TX (if any) still gets its TxEndEvent. An RX_WAIT node that is duty-cycle rejected stays in RX_WAIT with callbacks intact. After the sliding window has budget again, start_transmission returns a real tx id. Existing TDMA-deny empty-string behavior is unchanged.
